sections.heading: Our Process for Roof Leak Repair in Orange, NJ

c.v: The leak diagnosis starts at the interior stain

runs.v: , documenting the stain pattern on the ceiling and in the attic and measuring moisture in the surrounding materials. This interior evidence shows whether the leak is active during all rain, only during wind-driven rain from one direction, or only during freeze-thaw.

c.v: The interior evidence directs the roof inspection

runs.v: to targeted zones rather than a general walkover, so the team can inspect the flashing details that the roofing industry estimates account for 90–95% of leaks. On a flat Valley Arts or Main Street membrane, systematic moisture probing maps where wet insulation begins and ends, and controlled water testing confirms an inconclusive entry point. Roof leaks may require correcting flashing, drainage problems, or other underlying conditions to avoid repeated failures.

c.v: The repair specification follows the confirmed entry point

runs.v: , documented with photographs and matched to manufacturer specification with a written workmanship warranty. Efficient roof leak repair targets the root cause and matches the fix to the roofing material: replacing damaged shingles means removing the old shingles and securing a new one with nails and sealant, pitched-roof leaks reseal step and counter-flashing or replace a cracked pipe boot, and ponding leaks combine membrane patching with drainage correction. A post-completion water test verifies the permanent repair, separate from the manufacturer material warranty that covers factory defects.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace a Leaking Roof? The 25% Rule for Homes, Multi-Family, and Commercial Properties

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: When leaks and damage cover more than about 25% of the roof, a full replacement usually makes more sense than repairing the existing roof again, and on any building other than a detached one- or two-family home, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months requires a construction permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. Full roof replacement may be necessary when damage or deterioration is widespread, and historic homes may need a decking assessment during roof replacement.

asphalt shingles are the most popular roofing material, slate roofs can last over 100 years with proper maintenance, metal roofs reflect solar heat to improve energy efficiency, EPDM roofing systems are commonly used for flat roofs, and TPO is a popular choice for commercial flat roofs. faqs.q: I have a ceiling stain in my older Orange home but can't find where water enters from the attic. What's happening?

runs.v: Water in an older Orange home frequently enters at one detail and runs along framing before showing as a stain, so a Newark Quality Roofing diagnosis traces the path backward from the stain with moisture meters and, when needed, controlled water testing from the roof.

faqs.q: Water leaks into my Valley Arts loft building only during heavy rain. Is this a roof problem or a wall problem?

runs.v: Heavy-rain-only leaks on a low-slope loft roof often point to drainage capacity rather than a membrane failure: a flat roof needs at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to drain, per NRCA and ARMA, and when rain outruns the drains, water backs up over parapet caps and through seam overlaps. Wall leaks through siding, windows, or masonry can look the same inside, so the diagnosis water-tests the roof and the wall separately.

faqs.q: My Orange rental property has a tenant reporting a leak. How do you coordinate access?

runs.v: Newark Quality Roofing schedules interior and roof access under New Jersey landlord–tenant notice, then traces the leak from the unit where it emerges to the roof entry point. The work is documented with photographs for the owner's records and any insurance claim.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair a roof leak on my Orange home?

runs.v: New Jersey's Uniform Construction Code sets which roof repairs and replacements need permits: a repair of the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit, while repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building requires one. Properties in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the City of Orange office that handles construction permits before work begins.
